query: 2026 Tennessee Democratic gubernatorial primary latest news polling Jerri Green McCants August 6 2026
answer:
Research complete. The headline finding is that **this question is already resolved** — the primary was held August 6, 2026, nearly two weeks before today's date.

**Key takeaways:**

1. **Jerri Green won overwhelmingly**: 244,194 votes (69.0%), a 51.2-point margin over Carnita Atwater (17.9%). Kevin Lee McCants finished **third** at 5.4%. Results are complete across all 95 counties but unofficial until certification by **August 24, 2026**.

2. **The polling was catastrophically wrong in magnitude** — and there was only one poll. The Beacon Poll/TennSight (fielded April 20–27, released May 7) showed Green at just 14%, McCants at 11%, Atwater at 8%, with **62% "Not Sure."** Green's 3-point nominal lead became a 51-point rout. Prediction markets were far better calibrated: Polymarket had Green near 90% in early May.

3. **The general election is now the live question**: Blackburn (R) vs. Green (D) plus 13 independents on November 3. All pre-primary head-to-heads show Blackburn +21 to +24. All six race raters say Safe/Solid R. No general-election poll has been published since the primary. Green is outraised ~12.6:1 ($850K vs $10.74M).

4. **Post-primary news** (Aug 7–19): Trump endorsed Blackburn on Aug 7 after declining to pre-primary; Green has made Blackburn's debate refusal her central line of attack, releasing an ad on it around Aug 14–17.

Two data-quality caveats worth flagging: the TN Secretary of State had not yet posted the Aug 6 results to its historical-results page as of today (all totals come from aggregators reading the SoS feed, agreeing within ~0.2%), and the Polymarket/Kalshi tools returned no relevant Tennessee markets — the one market datapoint I have is secondhand via the Beacon Center.

key_facts: RESOLVED: The 2026 Tennessee Democratic gubernatorial primary was held August 6, 2026. Jerri Green won decisively with 244,194 votes (69.0%), a 51.2-point margin.

Full Democratic primary result: Jerri Green 244,194 (69.0%); Carnita Atwater 63,254 (17.9%); Kevin Lee McCants 18,961 (5.4%); Tim Cyr 14,796 (4.2%); Adam 'Ditch' Kurtz 12,456 (3.5%). Total 353,660 votes, 95 of 95 counties reporting.

Results are complete but UNOFFICIAL until county election commissions certify by August 24, 2026. Minor tracker variance exists (Decision Desk HQ as of Aug 13: Green 244,340 / 68.92%, total 354,520; Ballotpedia earlier snapshot total 347,884).
Decision Desk HQ called the race at 8:56 PM EDT on Aug 6 at >95% expected vote; AP called both gubernatorial primaries Thursday night Aug 6.

ONLY ONE public Democratic primary poll existed the entire cycle: Beacon Poll/TennSight, fielded April 20-27 2026, released May 7 2026, 400 RV subsample +/-4.8%: Not Sure/Other 62%, Green 14%, McCants 11%, Atwater 8%, Cyr 3%, Kurtz 2%.

The poll's error was enormous: Green polled 14% with a nominal 3-point lead and finished at 69.0% (+55 points of overperformance). McCants, the polled runner-up at 11%, finished THIRD at 5.4%. Atwater, polled third at 8%, finished second at 17.9%.
Prediction markets were far better calibrated than polling: Beacon Center noted in May 2026 that Polymarket had Green at nearly 90% to win the primary despite her 3-point polled lead.

Green carried 94 of 95 counties. Fayette County was the only county Atwater won (Atwater +10.2% per DDHQ). Green's weakest major-metro share was her home county Shelby at 63.8%; Davidson gave her 74.7%.

Republican primary same day: Marsha Blackburn won with 311,328-311,329 votes (43.4-43.6%), ahead of John Rose 235,511 (32.9%) and Monty Fritts 167,971 (23.4-23.5%) - an 11-point margin, far below her early ~50-point polling lead.
Democratic gubernatorial primary turnout (~353,660) was up sharply from ~258,000 in 2022. GOP primary turnout ~714,800 vs ~494,000 in 2022 (when Lee was unopposed).
Early voting: first two days ~77,000 ballots, +50% vs 2022 and +23% vs 2018; Democratic early turnout +82.1% vs 2022 and +39.4% vs 2018. Through July 23: 252,750 ballots (165,119 R / 81,732 D).

Jerri Green, 48, is a Memphis City Council member (District 2, since Jan 2024) and Shelby County's Interim/Chief Public Defender (appointed January 2026 by Mayor Lee Harris). B.A. UT Knoxville, J.D. Georgetown. Announced her campaign July 14, 2025. Slogan: 'One Tough Mother.'
Green's first campaign was the 2020 race for TN House District 83, where she won 46% against long-time Republican incumbent Mark White.
General election is November 3, 2026: Blackburn (R) vs Green (D) plus 13 independents (15 names total). Early voting Oct 14-29; voter registration deadline Oct 5.

This is the first time in Tennessee history both major-party gubernatorial nominees are women; whoever wins will be Tennessee's first female governor. Green is the first woman ever nominated for governor by the Tennessee Democratic Party.

All three pre-primary general-election polls show Blackburn leading by 21-24 points: Beacon Poll 5/7/2026 (1,157 RV, +/-2.7%) Blackburn 51% - Green 27%; Quantus Insights 8/8/2025 (600 RV, +/-3.5%) Blackburn 49% - Green 28%; Targoz Market Research (n=120) Blackburn 51% - Green 27%.
NO public general-election poll has been released since the August 6 primary (as of 2026-08-19). No pollster has ever published a favorability/approval number for Green.
All six major race raters have the general election as Safe/Solid Republican; none has updated post-primary. Cook PVI is R+14.

Campaign finance through Q1 2026 + supplements: Rose $14.97M (~$13M self-funded), Blackburn $10.74M, Green $850K (~$118K cash on hand). Green is outraised by Blackburn roughly 12.6:1. A pro-Blackburn PAC received $1M from Jeff Yass in April 2026.
Trump endorsed Blackburn on Truth Social on August 7, 2026 - his first endorsement in the race; he had declined to endorse before the primary.
